questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly, generous in spirit. 'Kind' is the closest synonym. 'Cruel' is wrong — it is the opposite (an antonym) of benevolent. 'Lazy' is wrong — it means unwilling to work, unrelated to benevolence. 'Proud' is wrong — it means having a high opinion of oneself, not related to kindness.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to 'ANCIENT':
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old or belonging to a distant past. 'Modern' (belonging to the present time) is its antonym. 'Old' is wrong — it is a synonym of ancient, not an antonym. 'Antique' is wrong — it means old and valuable, similar in meaning. 'Historic' is wrong — it means famous or significant in history, similar in context to ancient.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about synonyms:

(i) 'Happy' and 'joyful' are synonyms.
(ii) 'Big' and 'large' are synonyms.
(iii) 'Fast' and 'slow' are synonyms.
(iv) 'Begin' and 'commence' are synonyms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — happy and joyful both mean feeling pleasure. (ii) is correct — big and large both indicate great size. (iv) is correct — begin and commence both mean to start. (iii) is wrong — fast and slow are ANTONYMS (opposites), not synonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'GREGARIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Gregarious' means fond of company, sociable, enjoying being with others. 'Sociable' is the synonym. 'Solitary' is wrong — it means preferring to be alone (antonym). 'Hostile' is wrong — it means unfriendly or aggressive. 'Timid' is wrong — it means shy or lacking confidence.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Brave' and 'courageous' are synonyms.
Reason (R): Synonyms are words that have the same or nearly the same meaning.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — brave and courageous both mean showing no fear in facing danger. Reason (R) is also correct — the definition of synonyms is words with same/similar meaning. (R) explains (A) because brave and courageous fit this definition perfectly — they share the meaning of fearlessness. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the definitional basis for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their antonyms:

Column I:
(a) Generous
(b) Victory
(c) Temporary
(d) Humble

Column II:
(i) Permanent
(ii) Arrogant
(iii) Defeat
(iv) Miserly

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Generous (giving freely) ↔ Miserly (unwilling to spend) — matches (iv). (b) Victory (winning) ↔ Defeat (losing) — matches (iii). (c) Temporary (lasting a short time) ↔ Permanent (lasting forever) — matches (i). (d) Humble (modest) ↔ Arrogant (having an exaggerated sense of importance) — matches (ii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d). Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'OPTIMISTIC':
questions.explanation: 'Optimistic' means expecting the best outcome, being positive. 'Pessimistic' (expecting the worst) is its antonym. 'Hopeful' is wrong — it is a synonym of optimistic. 'Cheerful' is wrong — it means happy, which is related to optimism. 'Confident' is wrong — it means self-assured, which aligns with optimism.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs are antonyms?

(i) Diligent — Lazy
(ii) Affluent — Wealthy
(iii) Transparent — Opaque
(iv) Conceal — Hide

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Diligent (hardworking) and Lazy (not willing to work) are antonyms ✓. (iii) Transparent (see-through) and Opaque (not transparent) are antonyms ✓. (ii) Affluent and Wealthy both mean rich — they are SYNONYMS, not antonyms. (iv) Conceal and Hide both mean to keep secret — they are SYNONYMS, not antonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'ELOQUENT':
questions.explanation: 'Eloquent' means fluent, persuasive, and expressive in speaking or writing. 'Articulate' (expressing oneself clearly and effectively) is the synonym. 'Silent' is wrong — it means not speaking (antonym). 'Clumsy' is wrong — it means awkward in movement or speech. 'Ignorant' is wrong — it means lacking knowledge.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about antonyms:

(i) Antonyms are words with opposite meanings.
(ii) 'Hot' and 'cold' are antonyms.
(iii) 'Beautiful' and 'pretty' are antonyms.
(iv) 'Success' and 'failure' are antonyms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — antonyms by definition are words with opposite meanings. (ii) is correct — hot (high temperature) and cold (low temperature) are opposites. (iv) is correct — success (achieving a goal) and failure (not achieving) are opposites. (iii) is wrong — beautiful and pretty are SYNONYMS (both mean attractive/good-looking), not antonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'VERBOSE':
questions.explanation: 'Verbose' means using more words than necessary, long-winded. 'Concise' (brief and to the point) is its antonym. 'Wordy' is wrong — it is a synonym of verbose. 'Lengthy' is wrong — it means long, similar to verbose. 'Elaborate' is wrong — it means detailed, similar in concept to verbose.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Commence' and 'terminate' are antonyms.
Reason (R): 'Commence' means to begin, while 'terminate' means to end — they represent opposite points of an action.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — commence (begin) and terminate (end) are antonyms. Reason (R) is also correct — it correctly identifies their meanings and explains they are opposites. (R) explains (A) by showing the specific meanings that make them antonyms. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the proof. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'ABUNDANT':
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities, more than enough. 'Plentiful' is the synonym. 'Scarce' is wrong — it means insufficient in quantity (antonym). 'Limited' is wrong — it means restricted, opposite of abundant. 'Meagre' is wrong — it means inadequate, lacking in quantity (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Genuine
(b) Fragile
(c) Courage
(d) Rapid

Column II:
(i) Swift
(ii) Bravery
(iii) Authentic
(iv) Delicate

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Genuine = Authentic (both mean real, not fake) — matches (iii). (b) Fragile = Delicate (both mean easily broken) — matches (iv). (c) Courage = Bravery (both mean facing danger without fear) — matches (ii). (d) Rapid = Swift (both mean very fast) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'DILIGENT':
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means showing care and effort in work. 'Lazy' (unwilling to work or use energy) is its antonym. 'Hardworking' is wrong — it is a synonym of diligent. 'Careful' is wrong — it is similar in meaning to diligent. 'Attentive' is wrong — it means paying close attention, related to diligence.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Enormous' is a synonym of 'huge'.
(ii) 'Tiny' is an antonym of 'gigantic'.
(iii) 'Miniature' is a synonym of 'colossal'.
(iv) 'Vast' is a synonym of 'immense'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — enormous and huge both mean extremely large. (ii) is correct — tiny (very small) is the opposite of gigantic (extremely large). (iv) is correct — vast and immense both mean extremely large in extent. (iii) is wrong — miniature means very small, while colossal means very large — they are ANTONYMS, not synonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'METICULOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail, very careful and precise. 'Careful' is the closest synonym. 'Careless' is wrong — it means not paying attention (antonym). 'Reckless' is wrong — it means without thought of danger (antonym). 'Hasty' is wrong — it means done too quickly without care (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Frugal' and 'extravagant' are antonyms.
Reason (R): 'Frugal' means sparing or economical with money, while 'extravagant' means spending freely and excessively.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — frugal and extravagant are antonyms. Reason (R) is also correct — frugal means economical while extravagant means wastefully lavish. (R) explains (A) by defining both words and showing their opposing meanings. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the proof for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'TRANSPARENT':
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' means allowing light to pass through, clear, easily seen through. 'Opaque' (not allowing light through, not transparent) is its antonym. 'Clear' is wrong — it is a synonym of transparent. 'Visible' is wrong — it means able to be seen, related to transparent. 'Obvious' is wrong — it means easily understood, which aligns with transparency.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are pairs of synonyms?

(i) Accomplish — Achieve
(ii) Demolish — Construct
(iii) Prohibit — Forbid
(iv) Expand — Contract

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Accomplish and Achieve both mean to successfully complete something ✓ synonyms. (iii) Prohibit and Forbid both mean to not allow ✓ synonyms. (ii) Demolish (destroy) and Construct (build) are ANTONYMS ✗. (iv) Expand (make larger) and Contract (make smaller) are ANTONYMS ✗.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'OBSTINATE':
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means firmly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action. 'Stubborn' is the synonym. 'Flexible' is wrong — it means willing to change (antonym). 'Obedient' is wrong — it means complying with orders (antonym). 'Agreeable' is wrong — it means willing to agree (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The synonym of 'CANDID' is __________.
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward, open and honest. 'Frank' is the synonym. 'Secretive' is wrong — it means inclined to conceal (antonym). 'Dishonest' is wrong — it means not truthful (antonym). 'Reserved' is wrong — it means slow to reveal emotions, opposite of candid.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their antonyms:

Column I:
(a) Courageous
(b) Prosperity
(c) Transparent
(d) Generous

Column II:
(i) Stingy
(ii) Opaque
(iii) Cowardly
(iv) Adversity

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Courageous (brave) ↔ Cowardly (lacking bravery) — matches (iii). (b) Prosperity (wealth/success) ↔ Adversity (hardship/misfortune) — matches (iv). (c) Transparent (see-through) ↔ Opaque (not see-through) — matches (ii). (d) Generous (giving freely) ↔ Stingy (unwilling to give) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'INEVITABLE':
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen, cannot be prevented. 'Avoidable' (able to be prevented) is its antonym. 'Certain' is wrong — it is a synonym of inevitable. 'Definite' is wrong — it means clearly established, similar to inevitable. 'Unavoidable' is wrong — it is a synonym of inevitable.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Vivid' means clear and detailed; its antonym is 'vague'.
(ii) 'Serene' means calm and peaceful; its synonym is 'tranquil'.
(iii) 'Hostile' means friendly and warm; its antonym is 'aggressive'.
(iv) 'Mundane' means ordinary; its antonym is 'extraordinary'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — vivid (bright, clear) and vague (unclear) are antonyms. (ii) is correct — serene (calm) and tranquil (peaceful) are synonyms. (iv) is correct — mundane (ordinary, commonplace) and extraordinary (exceptional) are antonyms. (iii) is wrong — 'hostile' means UNFRIENDLY and antagonistic (not friendly); 'aggressive' is similar to hostile, not its antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'PRUDENT':
questions.explanation: 'Prudent' means acting with care and thought for the future, showing good judgement. 'Wise' is the synonym. 'Reckless' is wrong — it means acting without thought (antonym). 'Foolish' is wrong — it means lacking good sense (antonym). 'Impulsive' is wrong — it means acting without thinking (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Affluent' and 'destitute' are antonyms.
Reason (R): 'Affluent' means having a great deal of wealth, while 'destitute' means extremely poor and lacking basic necessities.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — affluent (rich) and destitute (extremely poor) are antonyms. Reason (R) is also correct — it correctly defines both words showing their opposite meanings. (R) explains (A) because the meanings demonstrate the opposition. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly proves (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'CONCEAL':
questions.explanation: 'Conceal' means to keep from sight, hide. 'Reveal' (to make known, uncover) is its antonym. 'Hide' is wrong — it is a synonym of conceal. 'Cover' is wrong — it means to place something over, similar to conceal. 'Mask' is wrong — it means to disguise or conceal (synonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct synonym pairs?

(i) Peril — Danger
(ii) Tranquil — Turbulent
(iii) Diminish — Reduce
(iv) Ascend — Descend

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Peril and Danger both mean a serious threat or risk ✓ synonyms. (iii) Diminish and Reduce both mean to make smaller/less ✓ synonyms. (ii) Tranquil (peaceful) and Turbulent (chaotic) are ANTONYMS ✗. (iv) Ascend (go up) and Descend (go down) are ANTONYMS ✗.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'LETHARGIC':
questions.explanation: 'Lethargic' means lacking energy, feeling drowsy and inactive. 'Sluggish' (slow-moving, lacking energy) is the synonym. 'Energetic' is wrong — it means full of energy (antonym). 'Active' is wrong — it means engaging in action (antonym). 'Vigorous' is wrong — it means strong and active (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Perilous
(b) Feasible
(c) Tranquil
(d) Arduous

Column II:
(i) Difficult
(ii) Dangerous
(iii) Peaceful
(iv) Possible

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Perilous = Dangerous (both mean full of risk) — matches (ii). (b) Feasible = Possible (both mean able to be done) — matches (iv). (c) Tranquil = Peaceful (both mean calm and quiet) — matches (iii). (d) Arduous = Difficult (both mean requiring great effort) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'ECCENTRIC':
questions.explanation: 'Eccentric' means unconventional, deviating from the norm, odd. 'Conventional' (following traditional standards) is its antonym. 'Unusual' is wrong — it is a synonym of eccentric. 'Strange' is wrong — it means weird/odd (synonym). 'Peculiar' is wrong — it means unusual/odd (synonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) The synonym of 'amplify' is 'enlarge'.
(ii) The antonym of 'amplify' is 'diminish'.
(iii) The synonym of 'amplify' is 'reduce'.
(iv) The antonym of 'amplify' is 'increase'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — amplify means to make larger/louder; enlarge means to make bigger (synonym). (ii) is correct — diminish means to make smaller (antonym of amplify). (iii) is wrong — reduce means to make smaller, which is an ANTONYM, not synonym. (iv) is wrong — increase means to make larger, which is a SYNONYM, not antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'INEVITABLE':
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen, cannot be avoided. 'Unavoidable' is the synonym. 'Preventable' is wrong — it means able to be stopped (antonym). 'Unlikely' is wrong — it means not expected to happen (antonym). 'Optional' is wrong — it means not compulsory (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Novice' and 'expert' are antonyms.
Reason (R): A novice is a beginner with little experience, while an expert is a person with extensive knowledge and skill in a particular field.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — novice (beginner) and expert (highly skilled) are antonyms. Reason (R) is also correct — it accurately defines both and shows their opposing levels of skill. (R) explains (A) by demonstrating the contrast. Option 2 is wrong because (R) proves (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The antonym of 'TRIUMPH' is __________.
questions.explanation: 'Triumph' means a great victory or achievement. 'Defeat' (failure to win) is its antonym. 'Victory' is wrong — it is a synonym of triumph. 'Success' is wrong — it is similar in meaning to triumph. 'Achievement' is wrong — it means accomplishment, aligned with triumph.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'BENIGN':
questions.explanation: 'Benign' means gentle, kind, or (in medical terms) not harmful. 'Malignant' (evil in nature, or cancerous/dangerous) is its antonym. 'Gentle' is wrong — it is a synonym of benign. 'Kind' is wrong — it is similar in meaning. 'Harmless' is wrong — it is a synonym of benign.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Zenith' (highest point) and 'nadir' (lowest point) are antonyms.
(ii) 'Apex' and 'zenith' are synonyms.
(iii) 'Summit' and 'base' are antonyms.
(iv) 'Peak' and 'pinnacle' are antonyms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — zenith (highest point) and nadir (lowest point) are classic antonyms. (ii) is correct — apex and zenith both mean the highest point (synonyms). (iii) is correct — summit (top) and base (bottom) are antonyms. (iv) is wrong — peak and pinnacle both mean the highest point — they are SYNONYMS, not antonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'VORACIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Voracious' means wanting or devouring great quantities (of food or information). 'Insatiable' (impossible to satisfy) is the synonym. 'Moderate' is wrong — it means average, not extreme (antonym). 'Content' is wrong — it means satisfied (antonym). 'Satisfied' is wrong — it means having enough (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their antonyms:

Column I:
(a) Expand
(b) Accept
(c) Create
(d) Ascend

Column II:
(i) Descend
(ii) Contract
(iii) Destroy
(iv) Reject

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Expand (grow larger) ↔ Contract (shrink) — matches (ii). (b) Accept (agree to receive) ↔ Reject (refuse) — matches (iv). (c) Create (make) ↔ Destroy (demolish) — matches (iii). (d) Ascend (go up) ↔ Descend (go down) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'LOQUACIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Loquacious' means very talkative, fond of talking. 'Taciturn' (reserved, saying little) is its antonym. 'Talkative' is wrong — it is a synonym of loquacious. 'Chatty' is wrong — it means inclined to chat (synonym). 'Garrulous' is wrong — it means excessively talkative (synonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs are antonyms?

(i) Attract — Repel
(ii) Captivate — Fascinate
(iii) Voluntary — Compulsory
(iv) Sufficient — Adequate

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) Attract (draw towards) and Repel (drive away) are antonyms ✓. (iii) Voluntary (done by choice) and Compulsory (required/forced) are antonyms ✓. (ii) Captivate and Fascinate both mean to charm/attract strongly — SYNONYMS ✗. (iv) Sufficient and Adequate both mean enough — SYNONYMS ✗.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'DETRIMENTAL':
questions.explanation: 'Detrimental' means tending to cause harm or damage. 'Harmful' is the synonym. 'Beneficial' is wrong — it means advantageous (antonym). 'Helpful' is wrong — it means giving help (antonym). 'Advantageous' is wrong — it means favourable (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Unanimous' means all in agreement; its antonym is 'divided'.
(ii) 'Amateur' means a beginner; its antonym is 'professional'.
(iii) 'Synthetic' means artificial; its synonym is 'natural'.
(iv) 'Obsolete' means outdated; its synonym is 'antiquated'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — unanimous (complete agreement) and divided (in disagreement) are antonyms. (ii) is correct — amateur (non-professional beginner) and professional (expert/paid) are antonyms. (iv) is correct — obsolete and antiquated both mean outdated/no longer used (synonyms). (iii) is wrong — synthetic (man-made) and natural are ANTONYMS, not synonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 'Ambiguous' and 'clear' are antonyms.
Reason (R): 'Ambiguous' means having more than one possible meaning and being unclear, while 'clear' means easy to understand without doubt.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — ambiguous (unclear) and clear (easily understood) are antonyms. Reason (R) is also correct — it accurately defines both words and shows their contrasting meanings. (R) explains (A) by demonstrating how the definitions oppose each other. Option 2 is wrong because (R) proves (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'EPHEMERAL':
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time. 'Transient' (lasting only a short time, not permanent) is the synonym. 'Permanent' is wrong — it means lasting forever (antonym). 'Lasting' is wrong — it means continuing for a long time (antonym). 'Enduring' is wrong — it means long-lasting (antonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'AMIABLE':
questions.explanation: 'Amiable' means friendly, pleasant, and likeable. 'Hostile' (unfriendly, antagonistic) is its antonym. 'Friendly' is wrong — it is a synonym of amiable. 'Pleasant' is wrong — it means enjoyable/likeable (synonym). 'Warm' is wrong — it means friendly in nature (synonym).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following words with their synonyms:

Column I:
(a) Affluent
(b) Futile
(c) Vigilant
(d) Profound

Column II:
(i) Deep
(ii) Wealthy
(iii) Watchful
(iv) Useless

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Affluent = Wealthy (both mean rich) — matches (ii). (b) Futile = Useless (both mean having no result/effect) — matches (iv). (c) Vigilant = Watchful (both mean alert and attentive) — matches (iii). (d) Profound = Deep (both mean very great or intense) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) 'Scarce' and 'rare' are synonyms (both mean not easily found).
(ii) 'Scarce' and 'abundant' are antonyms.
(iii) 'Adequate' and 'insufficient' are synonyms.
(iv) 'Ample' and 'sufficient' are synonyms.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — scarce and rare both mean limited in availability. (ii) is correct — scarce (few in number) and abundant (plentiful) are antonyms. (iv) is correct — ample (more than enough) and sufficient (enough) are similar/synonymous. (iii) is wrong — adequate means enough, while insufficient means not enough — they are ANTONYMS, not synonyms.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'TENACIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly to something, determined and persistent. 'Persistent' (continuing firmly despite difficulty) is the synonym. 'Weak' is wrong — it means lacking strength (antonym). 'Yielding' is wrong — it means giving in easily (antonym). 'Submissive' is wrong — it means ready to obey without resistance (antonym).
